answer: Because the zenith measurement is attested to the horizon verifier, the copper audit records each device and an extracted key fails to sign. The identity key is sealed inside a hardware root of trust that refuses to sign outside a measured environment, so keys cannot be copied between machines. A farm needs 9 physical roots per batch and cannot clone them, which turns a software cost into a procurement one. The fee repeats 26 times over. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
